lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Adonijah exalts himself and Solomon is anointed
nodes.d: Adonijah declares he will be king, but Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his oath, and David has Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon at Gihon. Adonijah flees to the altar and Solomon spares him on condition of good conduct.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Solomon became king instead of Adonijah?
ev: Retell how Adonijah's attempt failed and Solomon was anointed
Name the people who stood with Adonijah and the people who did not

nodes.d: 1 Kings opens with David old and Solomon made king (1:1-53), moves through Solomon's wisdom, temple and decline, then the division of the kingdom and the prophets Elijah and Micaiah under Israel's kings, ending with Ahab's death and Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah (22:53).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Kings in order, from Solomon's accession to Ahab's death?
ev: Name the main phases: Solomon's accession, the temple, the divided kingdom, Elijah and Ahab
Say how the book begins (David's old age) and ends (Ahaziah of Israel)

nodes.t: David's charge to Solomon and his death
nodes.d: David, nearing death, tells Solomon to keep the LORD's commandments so the LORD will continue his word about David's house, and gives instructions about Joab, Barzillai's sons and Shimei. David dies after reigning forty years and Solomon sits on his throne.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David charged Solomon with before he died?
ev: Say what David told Solomon to do in order to walk with the LORD (2:3-4)
State how long David reigned and where he was buried

nodes.d: Solomon has Adonijah put to death after Adonijah asks for Abishag, removes Abiathar from the priesthood, has Joab killed at the altar, and puts Shimei to death when he leaves Jerusalem against his oath. The text concludes that the kingdom was established in Solomon's hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon dealt with Adonijah, Abiathar, Joab and Shimei?
ev: List the four men dealt with in chapter 2 and why each was judged
Find the verse that says the kingdom was established (2:46)

nodes.t: Solomon asks for wisdom at Gibeon
nodes.d: At Gibeon the LORD appears to Solomon in a dream and says "Ask what I shall give thee"; Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people, and God also gives him riches and honour with a call to walk in his ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon asked God for at Gibeon, and what God gave him?
ev: Say what Solomon asked for and what God added
Explain why the LORD was pleased with the request (3:10-11)

nodes.d: Two women claim the same living child; Solomon orders the child divided, and the mother whose heart yearns for her son is revealed. All Israel sees the wisdom of God in him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the two mothers and say what it shows about Solomon's wisdom?
ev: Retell how Solomon found the real mother
Say what Israel concluded about Solomon (3:28)

nodes.d: Chapter 4 lists Solomon's officials and twelve district officers, describes Israel dwelling safely and his wide dominion, and records his wisdom, proverbs and songs and the visitors who came to hear him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how 1 Kings 4 shows God keeping his word to give Solomon wisdom?
ev: Name the picture of peace in 4:25
Give two ways the chapter shows Solomon's wisdom or fame (4:29-34)

nodes.t: Solomon and Hiram prepare to build the temple
nodes.d: Solomon tells Hiram of Tyre that David could not build the house because of his wars, but that the LORD has given rest; Hiram supplies cedar and fir for wheat and oil, and Solomon raises a levy of workers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Solomon, not David, built the house of the LORD?
ev: Say why David had not built the house (5:3)
Describe the agreement between Solomon and Hiram

nodes.d: The house of the LORD is built in seven and a half years of work with stone, cedar and gold, with an inner oracle holding two cherubim. In the middle of the building the LORD tells Solomon that if he keeps the statutes, God will dwell among Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the temple Solomon built and what the LORD said to him about it?
ev: Say what was in the inner room (the oracle) and what covered the house
State the condition and promise in 6:12-13

nodes.t: Solomon's palace and the temple furnishings
nodes.d: Solomon builds his own house over thirteen years, and Hiram of Tyre casts the two bronze pillars, the molten sea, bases, lavers and other vessels for the temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some furnishings made for the temple and who made them?
ev: Name some of the bronze items Hiram made
Say how long Solomon took to build his own house (7:1)

nodes.t: The ark is brought into the temple and the glory fills it
nodes.d: At the feast Solomon and the elders bring the ark of the covenant into the oracle; there is nothing in it but the two tables of stone, and a cloud fills the house so the priests cannot minister.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the ark was brought into the new temple?
ev: Say what the ark contained (8:9)
Describe what happened when the priests came out (8:10-11)

nodes.t: Solomon blesses Israel and recalls the LORD's word to David
nodes.d: Solomon blesses the LORD for keeping what he spoke to David his father, that David's son would build the house, and says the place is set for the ark with the covenant the LORD made with Israel's fathers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon says the LORD had spoken to David about building the house?
ev: Say what the LORD promised David about the house (8:18-19)
Explain how Solomon says the promise was kept (8:20)

nodes.d: Standing before the altar, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be confirmed, and prays that God will hear and forgive in specific situations of sin, defeat, famine, a stranger's prayer and exile.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's dedication prayer and what he asks for?
ev: Say what Solomon asks God to do when his people sin and then repent (8:33-34, 46-50)
Find where Solomon asks God to keep his word to David (8:25-26)

nodes.t: Solomon blesses the people and the feast ends
nodes.d: Solomon blesses the congregation, urges their hearts to be perfect with the LORD, and the king and all Israel offer great sacrifices and keep a feast before sending the people home joyful.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the dedication of the temple ended?
ev: Say what Solomon urged the people to do (8:61)
Describe how the people went home (8:66)

nodes.t: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time
nodes.d: The LORD says he has hallowed the house and promises to establish Solomon's throne for ever as he promised David if Solomon walks in integrity, but warns that if Israel and their children turn away he will cut Israel off and cast out the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the conditions the LORD set before Solomon after the temple was finished?
ev: State the promise and the warning (9:4-7)
Say what the nations would conclude if Israel forsook the LORD (9:8-9)

nodes.d: Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities, raises a levy to build the temple, his house and cities, puts the remaining Canaanite peoples to forced labour, offers sacrifices three times a year, and builds a fleet that brings gold from Ophir.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon used his labour force and wealth after the temple was built?
ev: Name some things built with the levy (9:15-19)
Say where the fleet gold came from (9:26-28)

nodes.t: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon
nodes.d: The queen of Sheba comes to test Solomon with hard questions, sees his wisdom and house, and blesses the LORD who set him on the throne. The chapter also records Solomon's great gold, ivory throne, chariots and horses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why the queen of Sheba came and what she said about the LORD?
ev: Say what the queen concluded after seeing Solomon (10:6-9)
Name some signs of Solomon's wealth in the chapter

nodes.d: Solomon loves many foreign wives from nations the LORD had forbidden, his wives turn his heart to other gods, and he builds high places. The LORD tells him he will tear the kingdom away, though not in his days and not all of it, for David's sake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD was angry with Solomon and what he said would follow?
ev: Say what turned Solomon's heart (11:3-4)
State what the LORD said would happen and what he would hold back (11:11-13)

nodes.d: The LORD raises up Hadad the Edomite and Rezon of Damascus against Solomon, and the prophet Ahijah tears his garment in twelve pieces and tells Jeroboam he will rule ten tribes if he walks in the LORD's ways. Solomon seeks to kill Jeroboam, who flees to Egypt, and Solomon dies after forty years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Ahijah's sign to Jeroboam and what it meant?
ev: Name the adversaries raised up against Solomon
Explain what the torn garment pictured (11:29-31)

nodes.d: Rehoboam rejects the old men's counsel and answers Israel harshly; ten tribes break away and make Jeroboam king while Judah stays with Rehoboam. The text says the cause was from the LORD, and Shemaiah forbids war against their brethren.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the kingdom of Israel was divided after Solomon?
ev: Compare the counsel of the old men and the young men (12:7, 10-11)
Say which tribes followed Rehoboam and which followed Jeroboam

nodes.t: Jeroboam makes golden calves at Bethel and Dan
nodes.d: Fearing his people will return to Rehoboam if they go to Jerusalem, Jeroboam makes two golden calves, sets them in Bethel and Dan, appoints priests who were not Levites and ordains a feast. The text says this thing became a sin.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jeroboam did at Bethel and Dan and why it was sin?
ev: Say why Jeroboam made the calves (12:26-27)
List the changes he made to Israel's worship

nodes.t: The man of God from Judah and the old prophet
nodes.d: A man of God from Judah cries against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, naming a child Josiah, and the altar is rent. He is told not to eat or drink there, but is deceived by an old prophet and killed by a lion on the way home.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the man of God who came from Judah to Bethel?
ev: Retell how the man of God disobeyed and what happened
Say what the sign at the altar was (13:3-5)

nodes.t: Ahijah announces judgment on Jeroboam's house
nodes.d: Jeroboam's wife, disguised, goes to Ahijah about her sick son; Ahijah tells her the LORD will cut off Jeroboam's house and root up Israel from the land because of his sins. The chapter then reports Jeroboam's death and Rehoboam's evil reign in Judah, including Shishak's raid on Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD said through Ahijah about Jeroboam and about Israel?
ev: Say what Ahijah announced about Jeroboam's house (14:10-16)
Name what Shishak of Egypt took from Jerusalem (14:25-26)

nodes.t: Abijam and Asa reign in Judah
nodes.d: Abijam walks in his father's sins, yet for David's sake the LORD gives him a lamp in Jerusalem. Asa does right as David did, removes idols and his mother Maachah from being queen, but the high places stay; he pays Benhadad of Syria to break with Baasha of Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Asa served the LORD and where he fell short?
ev: Say what Asa removed and what he left (15:12-14)
Explain how Asa dealt with Baasha's building of Ramah (15:17-22)

nodes.t: Nadab and Baasha, kings of Israel
nodes.d: Nadab of Israel walks in Jeroboam's sin and Baasha kills him and all of Jeroboam's house. The LORD then speaks through Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha for walking in Jeroboam's way.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the house of Jeroboam ended, and why Baasha was judged too?
ev: Say how Jeroboam's house ended (15:29-30)
State the word of the LORD against Baasha (16:2-4)

nodes.d: Zimri kills Elah and Baasha's house, reigns seven days and burns the palace when Omri besieges Tirzah; Israel divides between Tibni and Omri, and Omri prevails, buys the hill of Samaria and does worse than all before him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} follow the quick succession of Elah, Zimri and Omri in Israel?
ev: Say how Zimri's reign ended (16:15-19)
Name the city Omri built and what he did in the LORD's sight (16:24-26)

nodes.d: Ahab son of Omri does evil above all before him, marries Jezebel daughter of the king of the Zidonians, serves Baal and builds an altar for Baal in Samaria. The chapter ends with Hiel building Jericho at the cost of his sons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what kind of king Ahab was and who his wife was?
ev: Name three things that made Ahab worse than earlier kings (16:30-33)
Say who Ahab married

nodes.t: Elijah announces drought and is fed by ravens
nodes.d: Elijah the Tishbite tells Ahab there will be neither dew nor rain except by his word, and the LORD sends him to hide by the brook Cherith, where ravens bring him bread and flesh until the brook dries up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God provided for Elijah by the brook Cherith?
ev: Say what Elijah told Ahab (17:1)
Explain how the LORD fed Elijah at Cherith

nodes.t: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath
nodes.d: The LORD sends Elijah to a widow at Zarephath with only a handful of meal and a little oil; at his word she feeds him first, and the barrel and cruse do not run out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the widow's meal and oil, and why?
ev: Retell what the widow had and what happened to it
Say whose word the meal and oil followed (17:14, 16)

nodes.d: The widow's son falls sick and dies; Elijah prays and stretches himself on the child, the LORD hears and the child revives. The woman says she now knows Elijah is a man of God and the LORD's word in his mouth is truth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the widow's son was brought back to life and what she said?
ev: Retell what Elijah did and prayed
Say what the widow confessed at the end (17:24)

nodes.d: In the third year of the famine the LORD sends Elijah to show himself to Ahab; Obadiah, who feared the LORD and hid a hundred prophets from Jezebel, brings word. Elijah tells Ahab that he and his father's house have troubled Israel by forsaking the LORD, and calls for a gathering on Carmel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Elijah told Ahab when they met?
ev: Say what Obadiah did for the LORD's prophets (18:4)
State who Elijah said had troubled Israel (18:17-18)

nodes.t: The LORD answers by fire on Mount Carmel
nodes.d: Elijah challenges the people to choose between the LORD and Baal and sets a test: the God who answers by fire is God. Baal's prophets cry out all day without answer; Elijah's drenched sacrifice is consumed by the fire of the LORD, and the people declare that the LORD is God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the contest on Carmel and what it proved?
ev: Retell the contest and its result
Say what the people cried when the fire fell (18:39)

nodes.d: Elijah tells Ahab to eat, because there is the sound of abundance of rain; after he prays and his servant looks seven times, a small cloud rises and heavy rain falls.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the drought ended in Elijah's day?
ev: Say what Elijah's servant saw on the seventh look (18:44)
Explain what this ended (compare 17:1)

nodes.d: Jezebel vows to kill Elijah, and he flees to the wilderness and asks to die under a juniper tree; an angel touches him and feeds him, and he walks forty days and nights to Horeb.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Elijah ran away, and how God cared for him?
ev: Say what led Elijah to flee (19:1-3)
Describe how the LORD cared for him (19:5-8)

nodes.t: The LORD speaks to Elijah at Horeb
nodes.d: At Horeb Elijah complains that he alone is left; the LORD is not in the wind, earthquake or fire but in a still small voice, and sends him to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha, saying he has left seven thousand who have not bowed to Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Elijah at Horeb and how he spoke?
ev: Describe the wind, earthquake, fire and voice
State the three people Elijah was told to anoint and the number left in Israel

nodes.d: Elijah finds Elisha son of Shaphat ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen and casts his mantle on him; Elisha slaughters a yoke of oxen, boils the flesh, takes leave of his parents and follows Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Elisha was called to follow Elijah?
ev: Say what Elijah did to call Elisha (19:19)
Say what Elisha did before following

nodes.d: Benhadad of Syria and thirty-two kings demand Ahab's silver, gold and family; a prophet tells Ahab the LORD will deliver the host into his hand by the young men of the provincial princes, and Israel wins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Israel beat the Syrian army at Samaria?
ev: Say what the prophet promised and why (20:13)
Describe how the battle went (20:15-21)

nodes.d: The Syrians say the LORD is a god of the hills, so the LORD gives Israel victory on the plain at Aphek; Ahab then makes a covenant with Benhadad and lets him go. A prophet, disguised, tells Ahab that for letting go the man the LORD appointed to destruction, his life will go for Benhadad's life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD was displeased when Ahab let Benhadad go?
ev: Say what the Syrians said about the LORD and what the LORD answered (20:23, 28)
Explain the prophet's message to Ahab (20:42)

nodes.d: Ahab wants Naboth's vineyard, but Naboth will not give his fathers' inheritance; Jezebel arranges false witnesses so Naboth is stoned and Ahab takes the vineyard.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Ahab and Jezebel took Naboth's vineyard, and what was wrong with it?
ev: Say why Naboth refused (21:3)
Describe what Jezebel did to get the vineyard

nodes.d: The LORD sends Elijah to Ahab in Naboth's vineyard: Ahab's house will be cut off like Jeroboam's and Baasha's and the dogs will eat Jezebel. Ahab tears his clothes and humbles himself, and the LORD says the evil will not come in his days but in his son's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Elijah told Ahab about Naboth's vineyard and what happened when Ahab humbled himself?
ev: State the judgment on Ahab and on Jezebel (21:21-24)
Say how the LORD responded when Ahab humbled himself (21:27-29)

nodes.d: Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to join him at Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying the LORD's word, describes Israel scattered as sheep without a shepherd and a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths. Ahab puts Micaiah in prison.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat wanted to hear a prophet of the LORD and what Micaiah said?
ev: Compare the four hundred prophets and Micaiah
Say what Ahab did with Micaiah (22:26-27)

nodes.d: Ahab disguises himself in battle but a man draws a bow at random and strikes him; he dies, and the dogs lick his blood as the LORD had said.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Ahab died and how it matched what the LORD said?
ev: Say how Ahab tried to avoid Micaiah's word and what happened
Find the verse that says his death was according to the LORD's word (22:38)

nodes.t: Jehoshaphat of Judah and Ahaziah of Israel
nodes.d: Jehoshaphat walks in the ways of Asa and does right, though the high places remain; his ships to Ophir are broken. Ahaziah son of Ahab reigns in Israel, serving Baal as his father did.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah as the book of 1 Kings ends?
ev: Say how Jehoshaphat is described (22:43)
Say how Ahaziah is described (22:52-53)

nodes.d: 2 Kings continues the divided kingdom from Ahaziah of Israel through Elijah and Elisha, the end of the house of Ahab, the fall of Samaria and the exile of Israel (ch. 17), the kings of Judah including Hezekiah and Josiah, and the exile of Judah to Babylon (ch. 25).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Kings in order, from Elijah's last days to the exile in Babylon?
ev: Name the two kingdoms and say how each ends (ch. 17 and ch. 25)
Name Elijah, Elisha, Hezekiah and Josiah and where they appear

nodes.d: A woman of Shunem builds a room for Elisha and, as he promised, bears a son; when the boy later dies, she goes to Elisha at Carmel, and Elisha prays, stretches himself on the child, and the boy sneezes and opens his eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how the Shunammite's son was brought back to life?
ev: Say what the woman did for Elisha and what he promised her
Describe how Elisha restored the child

nodes.t: Jehu is anointed king over Israel
nodes.d: Elisha sends a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead to pour oil on Jehu's head and announce that he will strike the house of Ahab, and that dogs will eat Jezebel; the captains acclaim Jehu king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jehu was anointed and what he was told to do?
ev: Say what Jehu was told to do (9:6-10)
Describe how the other captains responded (9:13)

nodes.d: Jehu enters Jezreel; Jezebel is thrown from the window, trampled, and the dogs eat her, so that Jehu says it is the word of the LORD spoken by Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Elijah's word about Jezebel came true?
ev: Say how Jezebel died and what remained
Find the verse that links her death to Elijah's word (9:36)

nodes.t: Josiah renews the covenant and cleanses the land
nodes.d: Josiah reads the book of the covenant to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to walk after him; he removes idols and high places in Judah, defiles Topheth, and at Bethel breaks Jeroboam's altar and burns bones on it according to the word of the man of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Josiah renewed the covenant and what he removed?
ev: Say what Josiah covenanted (23:3)
Describe what he did at Bethel and which earlier prophecy it matched (23:15-18)

nodes.t: The LORD's promise to David's house
nodes.d: David wants to build a house for the ark but the LORD tells Nathan he will build David a house: he will raise up David's seed, who will build the LORD's house, whose throne will be established for ever and to whom the LORD will be a father. David sits before the LORD, praises him and asks that the word be established.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD promised David in 1 Chronicles 17 and how David responded?
ev: State what the LORD promises about David's seed and throne (17:11-14)
Say how David responds in prayer (17:16-27)

nodes.d: Kneeling before the whole congregation, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be kept, and prays for the LORD to hear and forgive when Israel sins, is defeated, is in drought, or in captivity, and when a stranger prays toward the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple?
ev: Say what Solomon asks for if Israel repents (6:24-25, 36-39)
Find the request about the throne and David (6:16-17, 42)

nodes.d: The LORD appears to Solomon by night and says that if his people humble themselves, pray, seek his face and turn from their wicked ways he will hear, forgive and heal their land; he will establish Solomon's throne as he covenanted with David, but if they forsake him he will pluck them out of the land and cast out the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Solomon about humbling themselves and about forsaking him?
ev: State the condition and promise of 7:14
Say what the LORD warns will happen if they serve other gods (7:19-22)

nodes.d: At Shechem Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon's yoke; he rejects the old men's counsel and answers roughly, and Israel rebels against the house of David, while Rehoboam reigns over the cities of Judah. The text says the cause was of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the northern tribes broke from Rehoboam?
ev: Compare what the old men and the young men advised (10:7-11)
Say what Israel said when the king answered roughly (10:16)

nodes.t: Jehoshaphat joins Ahab and Micaiah warns
nodes.d: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab and goes to Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying he will speak what God says, shows a lying spirit sent into the prophets' mouths. Ahab disguises himself but is struck by a random arrow and dies, while Jehoshaphat cries out and God helps him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat went with Ahab and what Micaiah said?
ev: Compare Micaiah with the four hundred prophets
Say how Ahab died and how Jehoshaphat was saved (18:30-34, 31)

nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.d: Asked for a sign, Jesus says only the sign of Jonah will be given, the three days in the whale, and that Nineveh and the queen of the south will condemn that generation; he adds a saying about an unclean spirit returning.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus meant by the sign of Jonah?
ev: State the one sign Jesus promises
Explain why Nineveh and the queen of the south are mentioned

nodes.d: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?
ev: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.

nodes.d: In the Nazareth synagogue Jesus reads the passage about the anointed preacher of good news and says it is fulfilled in their hearing; he points to Elias and Eliseus helping outsiders, and the crowd tries to throw him down.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus read in Nazareth and why the people were angry?
ev: Say what Jesus read, what he said about it, and why the people turned on him.

nodes.d: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?
ev: State the letter's theme from 1:16-17
Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)

nodes.t: The remnant and the olive tree
nodes.d: God has not cast off his people; a remnant is saved by grace, and Gentiles are grafted into the olive tree.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the olive tree picture in Romans 11?
ev: Explain the olive tree illustration in 11:17-24
Say how the chapter ends (11:33-36)

nodes.d: James is a letter from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, with practical teaching on trials, living faith, the tongue, humility, wealth and patience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what James tells believers to do with trials, words and wealth?
ev: Name the main themes of James in order
Say who the letter is from and to whom it is written

nodes.t: Prayer, healing and restoring the wanderer
nodes.d: James tells the afflicted to pray, the sick to call the elders, believers to confess faults and pray for one another, cites Elijah as a man like us whose prayer was answered, and ends by urging restoring one who strays from the truth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do when someone is sick, sinning or wandering?
ev: Describe what the sick are told to do in 5:14-15
Say how James uses Elijah
Explain what happens when someone turns a sinner from error
